boundary_note: Bounded first pass in the complete five-engagement frozen Burnside campaign. Opening populations and replacement boundaries are unresolved. NPS and an interested retrospective history supply attributed claims only; no predictors or causal command scores are admitted.

claims.value: Woodbury describes a garrison of about five hundred men; the live NPS table displays zero for both sides.
claims.rationale: An approximate garrison estimate, not a dated opening return or complete opposing pair. The live zero does not disprove that troops were present.

citations.locator: p.71, opening (OCR page markers; not checked against print)
citations.quote: garrisoned by a battalion of about five hundred men.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched opening populations. The frozen side-specific numerical bounds are blank; live zeros are not measured absence of troops. Retrospective formations, gun crews, garrisons, prisoners and troops engaged must not be interchanged.

claims.value: NPS describes a masonry fort commanding the channel to Beaufort; Woodbury describes low sand ridges sheltering siege work.
claims.rationale: Attributed physical context only. Siege positions may reflect command preparation, so no inherited/created classification is admitted.

citations.quote: a third system casemated masonry fort that commanded the channel to Beaufort

citations.locator: p.72, siege works (OCR page markers; not checked against print)
citations.quote: long, low ridges of sand, behind which the troops could work almost unmolested

claims.value: Woodbury reports delay from destruction of a railroad bridge, followed by arrival of ordnance and siege material after its completion.
claims.rationale: The bridge and siege preparation are attributed operational processes, not a readiness index or a commander effect estimate.

citations.locator: p.72, siege supply (OCR page markers; not checked against print)
citations.quote: Some delay had been experienced by the destruction of the railroad bridge.

citations.locator: p.72, same passage (OCR page markers; not checked against print)
citations.quote: large quantities of ord- nance stores and siege material began to arrive from Newbern.

claims.rationale: No original engineering survey, surrender correspondence, intelligence report or dated gun-condition record was inspected. Woodbury’s retrospective account does not establish either commander’s full knowledge state.

claims.value: Woodbury says Burnside decided on complete investment and a combined land and sea attack to force surrender.
claims.rationale: Attributed plan, not an inspected original instruction. Naval participation limits in the same source remain visible and success is not counted again as campaign contribution.

citations.locator: pp.71–72, investment (OCR page markers; not checked against print)
citations.quote: General Burnside therefore decided to make a com- plete investment of the fort, and, by a combined attack by land and sea, force its surrender.

claims.value: Woodbury assigns the land siege to Parke and identifies White as the defending commandant.
claims.rationale: Source-assigned roles, not reputation-based validation or automatic allocation of all credit. Lockwood’s naval role remains in the source context.

citations.locator: p.72, siege command (OCR page markers; not checked against print)
citations.quote: General Parke was an accom- plished engineer, and to him the work of besieging the fort by land w^as entrusted.

claims.value: NPS dates opening fire to April 26, while Woodbury dates Parke opening his guns to the morning of April 25. Woodbury’s later surrender-day numeral appears in OCR as 23th.
claims.rationale: Preserve the disagreement and garbled numeral without silently repairing OCR or changing the frozen March 23–April 26 interval. No precise surrender clock is established.

citations.quote: on April 26, opened an accurate fire on the fort

citations.locator: p.73, bombardment (OCR page markers; not checked against print)
citations.quote: Oh the morning of the 25th, General Parke opened his guns on the fort.

citations.locator: p.74, surrender (OCR page markers; not checked against print)
citations.quote: On the morning of the 23th, therefore, Colonel White hung out the white flag

claims.value: The frozen row and live NPS page record a Union victory.
claims.rationale: Same source family, not independent corroboration or a causal effect. Retain the frozen engagement interval and do not add a separate score for later occupation or campaign consequences.

claims.value: The frozen table gives 490 total (US 10; CS 480); the live NPS table displays 442 total (US 3; CS 439;).
claims.rationale: These versions remain distinct. No inspected return reconciles the totals, category definitions or reporting boundaries. Casualties are not opening strength or a predictor; a displayed zero is not evidence of no losses.

open_questions: Original orders, personnel returns, contemporary intelligence and source disputes remain deferred after the bounded shared-history follow-up. OCR has not been checked against print.
Keep opening, moving, engaged, garrison and captured populations distinct; do not use live zero displays as numerical evidence.
Broader blockade, occupation and later operations remain campaign context, not additional independent wins or automatic commander credit.
